title: Chinkapin Oak: Ancient Chinkapin Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: An oak of the American Midwest. In Indianapolis a chinkapin 617 cm round made the city bend its sidewalk around the trunk rather than fell it.
intro: The chinkapin oak is an eastern North American oak, and the ones we map grow in the Midwest and Tennessee, three of them champions of a state or county register. In Indianapolis the Temple Oak is 617 centimetres round, and when the city planned to straighten the sidewalk through it, the owners negotiated a cutout instead. Its age is put anywhere from under 300 to 450 years. Ann Arbor's park page calls the oak in Wurster Park the largest chinkapin in Michigan, and by girth the biggest tree of any species in town. In Milwaukee, near the northern edge of the species' range, the Wisconsin champion stands wider than it is tall. Nashville's has the longest memory, if not the surest name. The Tennessee register says it was already large when the battle of December 1864 crossed its farm, while one local group calls it a basket oak.
